context:
Run --unsafe-fixes once, then split the diff into directory-scoped commits for
reviewability. The Python default encoding is platform-dependent (locale on
Linux, utf-8 on macOS, mbcs on Windows) - adding explicit utf-8 is strictly
safer. For the few files that intentionally write CSV/TSV with platform
encoding, document and noqa per-line.
description:
Quality plan Phase 1a/1b/1d. The repo currently has 238 ruff violations, 235 of
them PLW1514 (open() without explicit encoding=). All are auto-fixable with
--unsafe-fixes. Apply the bulk fix in reviewed chunks, then ratchet the gates
so the gain is locked:
  - PLW1514 stays selected (currently selected - make sure CI fails on regression)
  - B904 (raise-from) added to ruff select as error
  - McCabe max-complexity lowered from 20 → 18, fix any new violations

This is a low-risk, high-signal cleanup that gives the rest of the quality plan
a clean baseline.

anti_patterns.dont: bundle the ratchet config changes with the bulk fix

anti_patterns.instead: fix or per-line noqa with reason

preserves.behavior: All currently-passing tests continue to pass
Existing per-file ruff ignores remain in place
No behavior changes - encoding="utf-8" is the safe default; only deviate where existing files document a different encoding

verifications.expected: All files would be left unchanged

work_units.summary: Run `uv run ruff check --fix --unsafe-fixes .` and review the diff in chunks (benchbox/, tests/, scripts/) - confirm encoding choices match file purpose (utf-8 for text, utf-8-sig only where needed)
Add B904 to [tool.ruff.lint.select] in pyproject.toml and fix any newly-surfaced raise-from violations
Lower McCabe max-complexity from 20 → 18 in pyproject.toml; refactor or noqa any newly-violating functions (with rationale)
Run full fast test suite + verify CI is green; commit ratchet config in a separate commit from the bulk fix so review is easy
